title: Referenced ID is assigned more than once
user_impact: Assistive technology cannot resolve the relationship unambiguously and announces the name or description of the wrong element.
technical_impact: The same ID occurs more than once in the DOM and is referenced by a for, headers or aria attribute.
source: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (review); HTML §3.2.6 the id attribute (unique in its tree); DOM getElementById / IDREF resolution
applicability: id values that an IDREF attribute (for, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-controls, headers, list, ...) in the same tree refers to.
expectation:
Asks for review at the second element carrying an id that occurs more than
once in the same tree and is referenced: the reference resolves to the first
element, and whether that is the intended one cannot be told from markup. A
duplicate id nobody references breaks no relationship (4.1.1 was removed in
WCAG 2.2): nothing to report. IDs are scoped per tree, so the same id in the
light DOM and inside a shadow root is not a duplicate. Applies whether the
reference is native (label for) or ARIA (aria-describedby). One review per
duplicated id.
